name: Instant noodles in Japan
summary: Momofuku Ando worked out at his home in Ikeda, Osaka, how to flash-fry noodles so that hot water revives them in two minutes; Chicken Ramen went on sale in 1958.
description: In a shed behind his home in Ikeda, Osaka, Momofuku Ando found that frying noodles in hot oil drove out their moisture, so that they kept for a long time and softened again in hot water. Chicken Ramen, which Nissin calls the world's first instant noodles, was launched on 25 August 1958; HISTORY.com reports more than 100 billion servings of instant noodles a year today.

impact.note: Instant noodles are eaten in many societies, above all across Asia, at about 100 billion servings a year; they are a more convenient form of an existing food, with a few direct successors such as cup noodles.

why: Ando had seen long queues at a ramen stall in post-war Osaka and, after losing his property in 1957, resolved to make ramen that could be prepared at home with only hot water.

date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: Momofuku Ando discovered the flash-frying process for drying noodles in 1958, according to Nissin.

evidence.supports: the technology that became the foundation of product development was the flash-frying process that Ando discovered in 1958

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated evidence found for this capability in this community. No review has yet confirmed that nothing earlier exists.

unresolved.note: The patent claim of Chang Kuo-wen (reported in weak sources as filed before Ando's and bought by Nissin in 1961) should be checked against a patent office record before it is discussed as an earlier invention.
The 100 billion servings figure is attributed by HISTORY.com to the World Instant Noodles Association; it is not checked against that body.
The claim to be the world's first comes from the maker; HISTORY.com's headline says "first mass-market".
The place of the launch is not given by the sources; the invention event is placed at Ikeda because the Nissin page puts the work shed behind Ando's home and his home in Ikeda City.

research.note: Nissin, HISTORY.com and Nippon.com all describe Chicken Ramen as the first instant noodles; an earlier patent claim by Chang Kuo-wen was found by the researcher only in weak sources and is not relied on.
